decision: REVISE — frozen decision_rule requires ALL C1-C5 for SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. C1 (100% success for both conditions) is stipulated as an analytical assumption, not measured: no LLM selection or resolution was executed, no binding failures observed (audit V1_C1_SUCCESS_UNMEASURED). The arithmetic portion of the frozen gate passes: C2 param selection tokens 16523 <= literal 19691 (16.09% reduction), C3 param total 18624 <= literal 19691 (5.42% net savings, 1067 tokens), C4 positive control 5 blog-read-post tasks collapse to 1 pattern with correct resolution, C5 null control ratio 1.0185 (1.85% overhead, well within 50% threshold). All arithmetic independently recomputed and verified exactly. However, C1 being an assumption rather than an observation is a measurement validity gap that prevents the frozen gate from passing. Additionally, completion tokens are hard-coded estimates (2 selection, 15 resolution, 20 cold) not measured from real model outputs — with 5.42% margin, modest variation in actual LLM response length could reverse C3 (audit V2_COMPLETION_TOKENS_ESTIMATED). Browser/verification costs omitted per frozen spec §5.1 but claim ceiling in report.md references 'end-to-end workflow savings' (audit V3_BROWSER_VERIFICATION). COLD baseline at 77 tokens/task is 8x cheaper than either registry condition but success rate unmeasured (audit V4_COLD_INVERSION). The producer SUPPORTS outcome is not justified as written because C1 was not measured and C3 margin is narrow under estimated completion tokens. The 5.42% analytical savings on this synthetic corpus is arithmetic-verified and informative but does not establish end-to-end workflow cost reduction.

Measurement validity violations (synthetic corpus, estimated completions, assumed success) prevent C-PRODUCT-ECON from advancing. next_question: Should the product lane (A) measure end-to-end workflow cost with real LLM selection and resolution calls on the existing synthetic corpus to resolve C1_success and completion_token gaps, (B) retry the deduplication measurement with the actual SPIDER registry/task corpus and kernel distill_parameterized() induction, or (C) close token-based inheritance economics entirely and pivot product lane to alternative mechanisms?
reason: The experiment's analytical measurement is arithmetic-verified and informative: 5.42% token savings exist on this synthetic corpus when selection+resolution costs are summed with estimated completions. However, three gaps prevent product conclusions: (1) C1 success was assumed, not measured — no LLM executed; (2) completion tokens are hard-coded estimates, not observed — 5.42% margin is thin; (3) browser/verification costs omitted from a claim about 'end-to-end workflow cost.' The COLD baseline being 8x cheaper than either registry condition is an unresolved economic concern that the producer acknowledges but does not address. The product lane faces a strategic decision: invest in measuring real workflow economics (option A or B) or close token-based inheritance economics (option C) given that the economic advantage of parameterized over literal is modest (5.42%) and does not survive comparison with the no-registry COLD baseline.
